classification.difficultyReason: Complete a frequency table, then restrict the sample space to one year group or combine two conditioning rows.

inlines.text: A school library surveyed students on their year group and their preferred study location. Some of the data is recorded in the two-way table below.
Use the given information to complete the table.

answer.worked:
Use row and column totals to obtain the six missing frequencies.
$$\begin{align*}n(\text{Year 8, Home})&=13-5-4=4\\n(\text{Year 9, Library})&=18-10-5=3\\n(\text{Year 9, Cafeteria})&=9-3-4=2\\n(\text{Year 9})&=3+2+6=11\\n(\text{Home})&=2+4+6=12\\n(\text{all students})&=15+13+11=39\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Find the probability that a student from Year 7 likes to study in the Library.

answer.worked:
Restrict the sample space to the 15 students in Year 7.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Library}\mid\text{Year 7})&=\frac{10}{15}\\P(\text{Library}\mid\text{Year 7})&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Find the probability that a student likes to study at Home, given they are not in Year 7.
Combine Years 8 and 9: 10 of their 24 students prefer Home.

answer.worked:
Students outside Year 7 are in Years 8 and 9.
$$\begin{align*}n(\text{Home}\cap\text{not Year 7})&=4+6=10\\n(\text{not Year 7})&=13+11=24\\P(\text{Home}\mid\text{not Year 7})&=\frac{10}{24}\\P(\text{Home}\mid\text{not Year 7})&=\frac{5}{12}\end{align*}$$
